# Entities

This folder catalogs the concrete, named entities that form the operational and clinical landscape of the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK) and the broader RKKP healthcare quality system. It encompasses the medical and administrative codes, pharmaceutical treatments, biomarkers, and digital systems used to track patient outcomes, alongside the organizations, health authorities, hospitals, and professionals responsible for governing and delivering care. By grouping these real-world actors, locations, and clinical tools, the wiki maps the entire infrastructure—from national registries and international guidelines down to specific municipalities and patient advocates—that drives cardiovascular quality improvement in Denmark.

## Pages

- [[entities/biomarkers/index|Biomarkers]] — Physiological markers like endocrine tests tracked in national quality indicators to identify underlying causes or comorbidities of cardiovascular conditions.
- [[entities/codes/index|Codes]] — Standardized medical and administrative coding systems, including ICD-10, ATC, and SKS codes, used to extract and measure healthcare quality data across Danish registries.
- [[entities/databases/index|Databases]] — Foundational national registers and healthcare registries that provide the demographic, diagnostic, and procedural data infrastructure for clinical quality reporting.
- [[entities/documents/index|Documents]] — Official reports, clinical tools, and academic publications that underpin quality development and patient education frameworks for atrial fibrillation care.
- [[entities/drugs/index|Drugs]] — Pharmacological entities, specifically anticoagulants, tracked via ATC codes to evaluate treatment adherence and clinical quality indicators.
- [[entities/groups/index|Groups]] — Collective entities and representative bodies, including patient advocacy groups and private cardiologists, that contribute to or advocate within the AFDK.
- [[entities/locations/index|Locations]] — Geographic and administrative subdivisions, from national aggregates to specific municipalities, used to benchmark and report clinical quality outcomes.
- [[entities/medical-interventions/index|Medical Interventions]] — Clinical protocols and structured educational programs monitored within the healthcare quality system to measure timely initiation and adherence to life-saving therapies.
- [[entities/organizations/index|Organizations]] — The multi-tiered organizational backbone of the Danish healthcare system, encompassing national health authorities, regional administrations, hospitals, and specialized clinics.
- [[entities/people/index|People]] — The interdisciplinary individuals, including health professionals, researchers, and patient representatives, who govern and guide national clinical quality initiatives.
- [[entities/pharmaceuticals/index|Pharmaceuticals]] — Pharmaceutical agents identified as clinical risk factors, such as NSAIDs and antiplatelets, with guidelines documenting their avoidance to prevent severe bleeding.
- [[entities/products/index|Products]] — Medical products referenced in the registry corpus, focusing on the comparative efficacy and safety monitoring of anticoagulation therapies.
- [[entities/standards/index|Standards]] — Formal frameworks, national classification codes, and international professional guidelines that govern clinical practice and quality measurement.
- [[entities/systems/index|Systems]] — Digital infrastructure and information systems, including shared hospital platforms and laboratory databases, deployed to register clinical data and monitor quality metrics.
- [[entities/websites/index|Websites]] — Official web domains and digital portals operated by health authorities and clinical quality organizations, serving as central administrative repositories.
